questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: For the experience - to try and live in a different country and meet people from all over the world.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to stay within Europe, and I really like the biking culture and how international Amsterdam is.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was a really nice experience overall. It was such a good way to meet people from many different countries, and try to live in a different country. 
The only thing that was a bit difficult was how many exams there are at University of Amsterdam (UvA), because you have a lot of small courses of 6 ECTS, and many of those have midterm exams too.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. UvA sends a lot of useful information on email, and they also did an online introduction for moving to Amsterdam and what you need to figure out in the beginning.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I attended the welcome introduction lecture, but did not use any assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got housing through the lottery system by UvA. It was a dorm form the company Lieven de Key, and it was located at Maassluisstraat in Niew-West. The process of getting the housing was quite stressful because you do not know if you will receive an offer until fairly late, and you need to act fast when you get the email through which you can book the specific housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is not really any housing at campus in Amsterdam, but it is fine to not live that central. If you get a bike (e.g. swapfiets) it does not take long to get to the center. And the route from Niew-West is pretty nice because it goes through Vondelpark.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is very easy to register for classes at UvA. You use the platform Glass, which is very simple, and it even show you how many spots are still available for the specific courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: In the online introduction for UvA they explained how to register for courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into which courses you can take in good time, so you are ready when the course registration starts.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was enrolled in the Exchange Programme for Behavorial and Social Sciences. The courses were generally interesting and there was a lot of interesting electives to choose between.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level of education at UvA was in general very good, though it did vary quite a bit between courses. Some of them were fairly easy while others could be quite demanding with a lot of mandatory tutorials, assignments and both midterm and final exams. 
The professors were really good at lecturing in general. They seemed passionate about their field of study

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar, but I think it is a bit more focused on tutorials at UvA. And they expect the students to participate actively a lot in those classes, which can both be fun but also demanding at times. There was also more mandatory classes and quite a few assignments in some of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
To get transferred as Work and Organizational Psychology:
- Lifelong Learning: personal, organizational and societal perspectives
- Current Topics: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion in the Workplace
- Education & Work

To get transferred as Advanced Research Design:
- Social Research Methodology

Elective course:
- Intersectionalities: Race, Gender, and Sexuality

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
My elective course "Intersectionalities: Race, Gender, and Sexuality" was such an interesting course, that I enjoyed thoroughly. The professor was very good, and we touched on discourses, social constructivism, colour-blindness, racialization, gender performativity (Judith Butler) and much more.
The course "Current Topics: Equity, Diversity and Inclusion in the Workplace" was also pretty interesting.
(I cannot recommend the course "Social Research Methodology". It had a big workload and they are very strict with grading).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Even though my phone should have the same data in thes rest of EU as in Denmark, it stopped working after 2 months, because more than half of the time within 4 months cannot be outside of Denmark, so that was an unexpected expense that I then had to get a dutch SIM and mobile subscription.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee was really expensive at most cafés. Eating out can also be very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is the USC sports club that is cheap for students, and they have a lot of different sports. I really enjoyed doing pilates classes there. And at Roeterseiland campus (the biggest UvA campus), there is the CREA café where some creative social events also take place.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
This place called Mezrab hosts open-mic story telling events on Wednesday’s which is a really fun experience. 
Besides that I also really enjoyed going to museums. With the museums pass that cost €75, you can get access to most museums across the Netherlands. There’s a lot of good ones in Amsterdam, but it is also nice when visiting other cities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travelling. There is a lot of nice cities in the Netherlands besides Amsterdam (e.g. Utrecht, Haarlem, Leiden, Maastricht). Besides that it also only takes a few hours to get to Belgium, Northern France or West Germany. There is so much to see, and it is very easy to find people to travel with. And solo travelling can also be a nice experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The culture is pretty similar to the Danish culture with biking, partying, people keeping to themselves, not being that formal with professors etc.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I do not think anything was challenging in regards to cultural differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The biking

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. There will be a lot of exams. It can be nice to look into what kind of exams (including midterms) your courses will have and prepare for the workload accordingly
2. There is no academic quarter at UvA
3. The resit exams for courses that end in December or January are not until in the Spring, so make sure to pass those.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are several campuses and depending on which courses you take you might have classes at two different ones in a row. So it can be difficult to make it in time. Biking is the fastest way to get from one to another.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other exchange students from all over the world. It is so interesting and fun to learn about each others cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a balance between exploring Amsterdam, travelling and studying

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
